_about: The simulation's and the launcher's settings. The launcher edits this file (./launcher config, or Settings in its interface) and checks every value; edit it by hand with the same care. Most values apply from the next start. Values marked informational are fixed by the engine and only described here.

_help.day: Day type (Run). Which demand profile the day follows: a working weekday, or a weekend's later, flatter one. --day-type overrides it for a run. Accepts: 0 (weekday), 1 (weekend). Default: 0. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.playback.duration_seconds: Length of a day (Run). Wall-clock seconds one simulated day lasts at 1× speed. 3600 plays a day in an hour. Accepts: a whole number from 60 to 3600 seconds. Default: 3600. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.playback.tick_rate: Starting speed (Run). How fast a run plays when it starts, as a multiple of the length of a day. The observer changes it while it runs. Accepts: a number above 0 and at most 10 ×. Default: 1.0. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.selection_mode: Where worlds are (Engine). Which cities a seed may choose: every city in the catalogue (379 on core-ng; Tools, Supported cities lists them), only the countries or cities in Places, or always the one city in Places. With every city, anything listed in Places still applies: two-letter codes are countries, other names cities. Anything but every city needs core-ng, which this turns on. Accepts: "global" (Every city), "countries" (Countries), "cities" (Cities), "fixed_city" (One city). Default: "global". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to Countries, it sets Engine to core-ng (default). Set to Cities, it sets Engine to core-ng (default). Set to One city, it sets Engine to core-ng (default). Set to Every city when Engine is set to core-legacy.
_help.map.places: Places (Engine). Countries (two-letter codes, such as IN, AE) or cities (IDs, such as mumbai, new-york), separated by commas. A - before one leaves it out: -IN is everywhere but India; IN, AE, -dubai is India and the UAE but not Dubai. all when worlds may be anywhere. Needs core-ng. In the launcher, Enter on this setting opens the list of countries to choose from. Accepts: text. Default: "all". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to all when Engine is set to core-legacy.
_help.sumo.enabled: SUMO (SUMO). Eclipse SUMO, for exporting a world and running it microscopically (POST /api/v1/export/sumo and /api/v1/system/sumo-simulate). Off, the server refuses both and does not look for SUMO. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.sumo.home: SUMO folder (SUMO). Where SUMO is installed (its SUMO_HOME). auto looks in SUMO_HOME, ~/sumo, Homebrew and the system's folders. Accepts: text. Default: "auto". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.max_nodes: Largest network (Map). The most junctions a district's road network may have. Lower keeps big cities light. Accepts: a whole number from 2 to 50000 junctions. Default: 50000. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.city_extent_m: City extract (Map). The side of the square of city downloaded around a seed's anchor. Larger holds more of the city and takes longer to download; the default is the one every seed's city was chosen with. Accepts: a whole number from 500 to 20000 m. Default: 5000. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.district_nodes: District size (Map). How many junctions the district grown from the anchor aims for, within the extract. Accepts: a whole number from 200 to 50000 junctions. Default: 3000. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.cache_policy: Map cache at start (Map). What the server does with the map cache as it starts: keep every city, prune to the most recent few, or clear it. Accepts: "prune" (Prune), "keep" (Keep), "clear" (Clear). Default: "prune". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.cache_keep: Cities kept when pruning (Map). How many of the most recently used cities pruning keeps. Accepts: a whole number from 0 to 1000 cities. Default: 1. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.download_stall_s: Download stall limit (Map). How long a map download may receive nothing before it is given up and the next server is tried. Accepts: a whole number from 10 to 3600 s. Default: 200. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.map.cache_dir: Map cache folder (Map). Where downloaded city extracts are kept, relative to the checkout. Dynamic Fastboot's next city is kept here too. Accepts: text. Default: "data/maps". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.traffic: Traffic demand (Modules). Base and hotspot demand on every road. Off, the roads stay empty. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.signals: Signal timing (Modules). Signal controllers at junctions, each on its own schedule. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.buildings: Places and trips (Modules). Demand drawn by schools, offices, shops and other places. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.dws: Weather (Modules). Rain cells, scheduled and called up by hand. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.flooding: Flooding (Modules). Standing water on low roads under rain, and the closures it causes. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.modules.news: News feed (Modules). A running feed of what happens in the district. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.dws.frequency: Storms a day (Weather). How many storms are scheduled across a simulated day. 0 leaves only those called up by hand. Accepts: a whole number, at least 0 storms. Default: 3. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.dws.storm_gap_s: Gap between storms (Weather). The least time between two scheduled storms' starts, in seconds of playback. Accepts: a number from 0 to 600 s. Default: 5. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.dws.storm_min_minutes: Shortest storm (Weather). How long the shortest scheduled storm lasts, in simulated minutes. Each storm's length is drawn between this and the longest. Accepts: a number from 5 to 1440 min. Default: 45. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.dws.storm_max_minutes: Longest storm (Weather). How long the longest scheduled storm lasts, in simulated minutes. Accepts: a number from 5 to 1440 min. Default: 120. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.bus_stops.min_spacing_m: Closest stops (Bus stops). The least distance along the roads between two bus stops the district is given. Accepts: a number from 50 to 5000 m. Default: 300. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.bus_stops.target_spacing_m: Usual spacing (Bus stops). The spacing stops are placed at where the roads allow. Accepts: a number from 50 to 5000 m. Default: 500. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.bus_stops.max_coverage_m: Farthest from a stop (Bus stops). No junction is farther than this from a stop; stops are added until none is. Accepts: a number from 50 to 10000 m. Default: 800. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.launcher.default_settings: Observer at its defaults (Launcher). Every launch opens the observer with its own settings back at their defaults, forgetting what this browser chose. --default-settings does it once. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies at once.
_help.launcher.command_bar: Command bar (Launcher). The prompt at the foot of the terminal interface, where commands are typed as in a shell, joined with | && || and ;. : or / goes to it. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies at once.
_help.launcher.scroll_lines: Scroll speed (Launcher). How many lines one notch of the mouse wheel or trackpad scrolls a list or the command output. Accepts: a whole number from 1 to 20 lines. Default: 3. Applies at once.
_help.launcher.natural_scrolling: Natural scrolling (Launcher). Content moves the way the fingers do, as on a Mac's trackpad. Off, the wheel moves the view instead. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies at once.
_help.launcher.small_terminal: Small terminals (Launcher). What happens when the terminal is too small for the full interface: ask (Simplified Launch Control, or leave), always use Simplified Launch Control, or show the full interface anyway. Accepts: "ask" (Ask), "simplified" (Simplified), "full" (Full anyway). Default: "ask". Applies at once.
_help.api.host: Listen address (Server). 127.0.0.1 keeps the server to this machine; 0.0.0.0 opens it to the network, which needs a gateway in front (see Deployment). Accepts: text. Default: "127.0.0.1". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.api.allowed_hosts: Other host names (Server). Host names besides localhost that may reach a server on this machine, separated by commas (DNS rebinding protection refuses the rest). none for none. Accepts: text. Default: "none". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.api.allowed_origins: Other origins (Server). Web origins besides the server's own that may change things, separated by commas, such as https://example.org. none for none. Accepts: text. Default: "none". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.api.port: Port (Server). The port to listen on. If it is taken, the next free one is used, and the launcher says which. Accepts: a whole number from 1 to 65535. Default: 8090. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.narration.mode: Realistic News (Server). Who writes the news: auto uses Apple Foundation Models where this Mac has them, else a model server on this machine (Ollama, LM Studio), never a cloud provider; model uses the launcher's own model, cloud providers included (each news item is a request); fm insists on Apple's; off keeps the plain wording; or give a Chat Completions endpoint (http://HOST:PORT, unix:/PATH). --narrator overrides it. Accepts: text. Default: "auto". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.applications: Applications may connect (Fabric). Programs may register through the Fabric API. Off, nothing can, and WebFabric is off too. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to disabled, it sets WebFabric to disabled. Set to enabled when WebFabric is set to enabled.
_help.fabric.legacy_api: Legacy routes (Fabric). The older /playback and /control routes still answer. They take no credential, so turning them off leaves only the Fabric API. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.launch_proposals: Launch proposals (Fabric). Applications may propose how to start them, for a person to read and approve here. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.require_signatures: Signed requests only (Fabric). Every application must sign every request with its key (HMAC-SHA-256), not only present its token. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.world_regeneration: New worlds from the observer (Fabric). A person in the observer may ask for a new world. The seed is still the server's choice. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_frames: Embedded pages (Fabric). Applications may show a page of their own inside the observer, sandboxed, from the origins they declare. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_dialogs: Dialogs (Fabric). Applications may ask a person a question in a dialog. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_camera: Camera direction (Fabric). Applications may ask the map to look somewhere, once a person allows it. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_layers: Layer control (Fabric). Applications may hold map layers and places on or off, once a person allows it. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_control: Simulation control (Fabric). Applications may play, pause, seek and change the run, once a person allows it. Every action is on the audit log. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_notifications: Notifications (Fabric). Applications may send notifications, within a rate limit. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_messages: Messages between applications (Fabric). Applications may send each other messages. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.fabric.allow_storage: Storage (Fabric). Applications may keep a little data of their own across restarts. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.webfabric.enabled: WebFabric (WebFabric). Applications' panels, controls and overlays appear in the observer. Off, they can still connect, but nothing of theirs is shown. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to disabled when Applications may connect is set to disabled. Set to enabled, it sets Applications may connect to enabled.
_help.startup.dynamic_fastboot: Dynamic Fastboot (Startup). While a world runs, the next one is chosen, in another city, and its map fetched in the background. A new world, or the next start, then takes seconds; only the first ever start downloads while you wait. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.startup.dynamic_particles: Adaptive start-up film (Startup). The film plans itself by the server's estimate of when the world will be ready: as many scenes as fit, in a new order, then straight to the map. Turns Play the whole film off. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to enabled, it sets Play the whole film to disabled. Set to disabled when Play the whole film is set to enabled.
_help.startup.fast_boot: Fast Boot (Startup). Use every city downloaded in advance (./launcher fastboot download), and open with the name alone. Turns Play the whole film off. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to enabled, it sets Play the whole film to disabled. Set to disabled when Play the whole film is set to enabled.
_help.startup.force_animate: Play the whole film (Startup). Every scene of the start-up film plays before the map, even when the world is ready sooner. Turns the adaptive film and Fast Boot off. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start). Set to disabled when Adaptive start-up film is set to enabled. Set to enabled, it sets Adaptive start-up film to disabled. Set to disabled when Fast Boot is set to enabled. Set to enabled, it sets Fast Boot to disabled.
_help.presentation.music: Music (Presentation). An original score while the start-up film plays, with a button to mute it. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.presentation.fullscreen: Full screen (Presentation). Open the observer full screen, in a window of its own. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.presentation.music_volume: Music volume (Presentation). From 0 (silent) to 1. Accepts: a number from 0 to 1. Default: 0.6. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.presentation.music_file: Music file (Presentation). What the start-up film plays: score for the written score, or an MP3, M4A or WAV file (a path in this checkout, or an absolute one). Accepts: text. Default: "score". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.demo.music: Music in Demo Mode (Demo). Demo Mode plays its score. --no-music turns it off once. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.demo.music_file: Demo Mode music file (Demo). What Demo Mode plays: score for the written score, or an MP3, M4A or WAV file. Accepts: text. Default: "score". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.demo.fullscreen: Full screen in Demo Mode (Demo). Demo Mode opens full screen. --no-fullscreen opens it in a window once. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.demo.scenes: Demo scenes and order (Demo). Which scenes Demo Mode plays, and in what order. Space turns one on or off, Shift+↑↓ moves it. The name always opens the loop. As text: ids separated by commas. Accepts: text. Default: "streets, signals, demand, rush-hour, incidents, weather, cities, repeatable, auto-focus, webfabric, time-control, many-worlds, ai-ready". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.compression: Compression (Performance). How hard the server compresses large replies. Fast costs least processor time; small saves bytes on a slow link; off sends them as they are. Accepts: "fast" (Fast), "balanced" (Balanced), "small" (Small), "off" (Off). Default: "fast". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.api_threads: Request threads (Performance). How many requests the server answers at once. 0 lets it choose from the processor count. Accepts: a whole number from 0 to 256. Default: 0. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.engine_threads: Snapshot threads (Performance). Threads that write a large snapshot in parallel. 0 lets it choose; 1 keeps it to one. Accepts: a whole number from 0 to 64. Default: 0. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.map_fps: Map frame rate (Performance). How often the map's moving traffic is redrawn. Automatic drops to 30 a second when the map struggles. Accepts: 0 (Automatic), 60 (60 a second), 30 (30 a second). Default: 0. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.render_scale: Render scale (Performance). The most pixels the map draws per point on a high-density screen. Lower is lighter on the graphics processor. Accepts: a number from 0.5 to 3. Default: 2. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.playback.checkpoint_virtual_seconds: Checkpoint spacing (Performance). How often a run keeps a checkpoint, in simulated seconds. Closer makes seeking back faster and takes more memory; it never changes results. Accepts: a whole number from 60 to 3600 s. Default: 900. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.performance.film_particles: Film particles (Performance). How many particles the start-up film draws. Fewer is lighter; a struggling page draws fewer by itself. Accepts: a whole number from 4000 to 32000. Default: 32000. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.mcp.enabled: MCP Handler (MCP). An AI client may connect through the Model Context Protocol (./launcher mcp serve) and read. No agent is included: this opens the door, which is closed by default. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies when an MCP client next connects. Set to enabled when AI may change things is set to enabled. Set to enabled when AI may start and stop runs is set to enabled. Set to disabled, it sets AI may change things to disabled. Set to disabled, it sets AI may start and stop runs to disabled.
_help.mcp.allow_writes: AI may change things (MCP). An AI client may call routes that change the simulation (POST, PUT, DELETE). Turns the MCP Handler on. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies when an MCP client next connects. Set to enabled, it sets MCP Handler to enabled. Set to disabled when MCP Handler is set to disabled.
_help.mcp.allow_launcher: AI may start and stop runs (MCP). An AI client may start and stop simulations and change settings through the launcher. Turns the MCP Handler on. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies when an MCP client next connects. Set to enabled, it sets MCP Handler to enabled. Set to disabled when MCP Handler is set to disabled.
_help.model.provider: Model (Model). Which model answers requests in plain words, here and wherever DSTNS asks one. Automatic uses Apple's Foundation Models where this Mac has them; else a model server on this machine (Ollama, LM Studio); else each cloud provider with a key (model key PROVIDER KEY) in turn. Accepts: "auto" (Automatic), "apple" (Apple Foundation Models), "ollama" (Ollama), "lmstudio" (LM Studio), "anthropic" (Anthropic), "openai" (OpenAI), "gemini" (Google Gemini), "groq" (Groq), "mistral" (Mistral), "openrouter" (OpenRouter), "huggingface" (Hugging Face), "custom" (Another Chat Completions server), "off" (Off). Default: "auto". Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.name: Model name (Model). Which model of the chosen provider (model list shows them). default uses each provider's own. Accepts: text. Default: "default". Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.base_url: Provider address (Model). Where the chosen provider answers, for a server of your own or a regional endpoint; needed for Another Chat Completions server. default uses the provider's own. Accepts: text. Default: "default". Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.ollama_url: Ollama address (Model). Where Ollama answers. Accepts: text. Default: "http://127.0.0.1:11434". Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.apple_cloud: Private Cloud Compute (Model). When Apple's model on this Mac cannot answer, use Apple's larger model through Private Cloud Compute (macOS 27 or later). Requests leave the Mac for Apple's servers, which keep nothing. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.key_store: Where keys are kept (Model). Where model key keeps a provider's API key: config/launcher.env on this machine, or the system's credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux). Keys in the environment are always read too. Accepts: "env" (config/launcher.env), "system" (System credential store). Default: "env". Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.worlds.keep_history: Keep history across worlds (Run). Off, a new world starts clean: the observer's notification history and the launcher's conversation with its model begin again, as the report and its list of jumps always do. On, both carry over from one world to the next. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.assist.enabled: Answers for other programs (Model). Other programs may ask about DSTNS too: the MCP tool dstns_ask (when the MCP Handler is on) and POST /v1/assist on CoreAI's service. Answers only inform; nothing is run or changed. The command bar and ask always answer. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.model.timeout_seconds: Model time limit (Model). How long to wait for a model's answer before trying the next or giving up. Accepts: a whole number from 5 to 600. Default: 60. Applies at the next request to a model.
_help.daemon.enabled: Daemons (Daemons). Small watchers inside the server: the Resource Control Subsystem, memory, disk, a stalled run, and the cache handler. They say what they notice in the launcher and the observer, and on the daemon queues for applications. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.sustain_s: Hold before alerting (Daemons). How long a condition must hold before a daemon says anything, so that a brief spike is not an alarm. Accepts: a number from 0 to 300 s. Default: 5. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.rcs: Resource Control Subsystem (Daemons). Each module's memory and processor against its α, β and γ (Resource Control). Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.memory: Memory watch (Daemons). The machine's available memory: a warning when it is low, an emergency when it is critical. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.disk: Disk watch (Daemons). Free space where the logs and maps are kept. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.stall: Stall watch (Daemons). A run that should be running but whose clock has stopped. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.daemon.cache: Auto cache handler (Daemons). Clears what nothing needs: old cities beyond the cache's budget, abandoned downloads, stray files. Never the running world's city or the next one. Accepts: true or false. Default: true. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.cache.max_mib: Map cache budget (Daemons). The most the map cache may hold; the cities least recently used go first. Accepts: a whole number from 0 to 1048576 MiB. Default: 2048. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.cache.interval_min: Cache sweep every (Daemons). How often the cache handler looks; it also looks at once when disk space is low. Accepts: a whole number from 1 to 1440 min. Default: 10. Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.engine.memory: Engine memory (Resource Control). α, β, γ in MiB: the least the engine should use while it works, where it is using a lot (a warning), and the most it ever should (an alert). Accepts: text. Default: "4, 2048, 4096". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.engine.cpu: Engine processor (Resource Control). α, β, γ as a percentage of one core. Below α while the run is running, something may be wrong. Accepts: text. Default: "0.2, 180, 380". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.downloads.memory: Map downloads memory (Resource Control). α, β, γ in MiB, for the map downloads while they run. Accepts: text. Default: "0, 768, 2048". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.downloads.cpu: Map downloads processor (Resource Control). α, β, γ as a percentage of one core. Accepts: text. Default: "0, 150, 300". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.launcher.memory: Launcher memory (Resource Control). α, β, γ in MiB, for this launcher. Accepts: text. Default: "1, 256, 1024". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.launcher.cpu: Launcher processor (Resource Control). α, β, γ as a percentage of one core. Accepts: text. Default: "0, 60, 150". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.applications.memory: Applications memory (Resource Control). α, β, γ in MiB, for the applications this launcher starts, together. Accepts: text. Default: "0, 1024, 4096". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.rcs.applications.cpu: Applications processor (Resource Control). α, β, γ as a percentage of one core, together. Accepts: text. Default: "0, 200, 400". Applies from the next start of the server (./launcher start).
_help.security.advanced: Advanced Security (Security). The launcher asks for Touch ID or your system password as it opens, and before any single command that changes something. No program can change the launcher or the engine through the MCP Handler. Turning it off asks again. Accepts: true or false. Default: false. Applies at once.
